newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki up as finance shares offset Nokia fall.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki up as finance shares offset Nokia fall.

text.p: Telecoms blue-chip Nokia eased amid profit-taking on Monday, but the Finnish bourse managed a small gain on the HEX all-share index thanks to rallying finance sector shares and a modest rise in forestries.
The HEX index advanced for the third straight session, closing a meagre 0.1 percent higher at 2,369.94. But it closed below last Friday's all-time high 2,399.03 set in intra-day trade.
Turnover was quite lively at 460 million markka with deals in Nokia accounting for 40 percent.
Hit by profit-taking in reaction to sharp gains last week when the company reported third-quarter earnings in line with forecasts, Nokia ended 1.00 markka lower at 255.50 markka.

Usually the HEX index trend equals that of Nokia but on Monday Nokia's losses were offset by strength in finance sector shares, which joined a rally in Swedish finance stocks following rumours about S-E-Banken buying Nordbanken, brokers said.
Merita -- Finland's biggest banking group -- closed 0.20 markka higher at 14.40 after hitting 14.50 -- its highest since June 22, 1995. Insurers Pohjola and Sampo also gained.
Some forest industry shares found comfort in news that a six-month fall in paper export prices had ended in October. Enso ended 0.40 markka higher at 35.90.
